title: Trim
teaser: A weight-loss dashboard that turns your own Google Sheet into a weekly trend, with an optional AI coach.

sections.problem: I started a fitness program a few years ago with the aim of losing a few pounds. My personal aim was to track signals surrounding me that were influencing my goal positively or negatively. With a lot of data recorded, it made sense to me that some of what was missing was succinct summaries, conclusions against my signals, and a test to see if I could bring AI in to help synthesize all of the factors.
sections.build: A weekly-anchored dashboard that reads directly from one or more Google Sheets (public CSV export links, no API keys) and joins them by date into KPIs, a trend chart, and a Y/N daily-goal compliance card. Weeks are the atomic unit everywhere, not a rolling window, the current in-progress week shows a live count but withholds comparisons until it's actually complete. An optional Coach feature shells out locally to the Claude Code CLI to write a weekly verdict and recommendation, checking recent weeks of history before writing a new one. A Profile tab holds the person's own story and targets, and five style dials (warmth, delivery, directiveness, pace, and accountability) set how the coach sounds and how hard it pushes.
sections.technical: A small Express server with no database, reading local JSON config and fetching Google Sheets CSV exports server-side. The dashboard itself has no built-in LLM calls; the one AI feature runs the Claude Code CLI headlessly on the user's own machine when they click Analyze Week, sending that week's data, an all-time progress summary, the user's profile and weekly notes, and recent recommendations to Anthropic under the user's own account. The five style dials are compiled into the coach's prompt at that moment, so the same data can be coached in different voices. Nothing else leaves the machine apart from the Google Sheets fetch. The public demo is a self-contained static build with fictional data, no server or Sheets connection needed to view it.
sections.learning: The agentic position on this app is pretty robust in terms of thinking through what all I should need to send in as context to be rationalized. Figuring out how I wanted to go about generating an agentic recommendation and then turn to feed a certain volume of them back in later periods to reinforce the ecosystem of activity was an exciting opportunity to dig further into.
sections.next: With the coach's voice and the interface settled, the next thing I want to explore is whether the signals a person tracks start to show patterns together over time. Weight is the headline, but steps, calories, and other signals all move alongside it, and today the app shows their shapes without saying whether they're related. I want to compute that properly, comparing each signal with weight change across weeks and across short lags, and only surface a "possible pattern" once there's enough history to support it. The coach would receive those findings as evidence to weigh against the person's own story, not as a verdict. The aim is a coach that notices what's actually working for this person, without ever claiming more than the data can say.
